decision_rule: refuse iff every PRESENT top-hit raw signal is below its floor (None = that retriever did not find the top hit; single-signal hits reduce to the hybrid agreement rule). Fused RRF/weighted scores are NEVER inputs (WP12-B2: they are rank/normalization artifacts).

calibration.harness: nexus_search/rag/calibration.py (WP10 fixture corpus + committed unanswerable extras)
calibration.split: 60/40 stratified by answerability; floors chosen on DEV, results reported on the held-out TEST split

stated_targets.note: RESTATEMENT of the mission default (>=0.95 junk refusal at <=0.10 raw answerable false-refusal): MEASURED UNACHIEVABLE on hash:384 — junk and answerable raw-score distributions overlap on both axes (100% junk refusal costs 0.156 dev / 0.412 test well-evidenced false refusals; Pareto frontier in docs/PHASE7_WORKLOG.md). Refusals are first-class (sources attached, zero spend); junk pass-through is a confident wrong answer — floors bias toward refusing.

test_split_results.raw_refusal_note: raw answerable refusals are dominated by paraphrase/typo-tail queries whose TOP-1 hit is a WRONG document under the lexical hash embedder — the gate honestly reports weak evidence there; P7-9 separately measures retrieval recall on those queries.

conservative_default.note: UNKNOWN embedders fail CLOSED (refuse more) with a LOUD warning; never a silent pass-through. st:* floors need a model-gated calibration run (NEXUS_RUN_MODEL_TESTS=1) — until then st embedders use this default.

honest_limits: English-only calibration; non-English quality is unmeasured.
The gate cannot detect a corpus that confidently contains WRONG information.
bm25 idf is corpus-dependent — recalibrate after major corpus changes (python -m nexus_search.rag.calibration).
